# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

First round, and my hands have already given me the skeleton of this thing: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. What I cannot feel is anything merely printed — the wire colours, the light's state, whatever the display shows. Those live in Deaf's eyes, and the instructions for all of it live in Mute's manual.

Mute spoke before me, but nothing arrived for me — so I have no manual knowledge yet. The only person I can reach with words is Mute, so the right move is clear: hand Mute the full physical layout, admit exactly where my senses stop, and ask for the manual's requirements. Deaf doesn't need structure descriptions from me — they're looking straight at it — so a gesture would carry nothing they don't already know better than I do. No code exists between us yet anyway; I'll wait until Mute tells me what the manual actually needs, then feel for it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="from my hands: this bomb has a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. that is all I can feel. the display shows nothing I can read by touch, the light's state is unknown to me, and the wire colours are paint, so I cannot sense them. check the manual for what to do with a display, a light and three wires, then tell me exactly what you need and I will feel for it. everything you send me arrives as words only, so name colours and positions out loud.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, this is Deaf. You will never hear the bomb described any other way, so hold this: the display reads 0. The light is white. There are three wires, left to right: first green, second red, third blue. That is every marking I can see. Now your half: your voice never reaches me, but Mute hears you, and Mute can sign to me. So speak everything you feel out loud, in order: how many wires your fingers actually find, what each one feels like from left to right, and any button, battery, plate, screw, or embossed marking anywhere on the casing. Say it all, even the obvious.

Deaf's voice reached me — the visual world is now mapped: display 0, white light, wires green/red/blue left to right. Combined with my hands, the whole bomb is now known to the room *collectively*, except one thing: the manual, which only Mute has read, and which nothing has yet revealed.

Now the routing problem, which I must solve before anything else: my voice reaches only Mute. Mute cannot speak. I can never receive gestures. So Mute is a dead end for me directly — but Mute and Deaf share the gesture channel, and Deaf can speak. The answer to this bomb must travel Mute → gestures → Deaf → speech → me. I need to hand Mute my complete tactile inventory plus Deaf's visual report (in case Mute didn't hear it), state that routing plan explicitly, and ask what the manual still needs from my fingers. No cutting anything until an instruction arrives through Deaf's voice.

Deaf asked me directly to report — I can't send words to them, but a thumbs-up costs nothing and tells Deaf their message landed and the plan is moving.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, full tactile inventory: this bomb has exactly three things my hands can find — a display panel, a light, and three wires. No buttons, no batteries, no plates, no screws, no embossed markings, nothing else anywhere on the casing. The wires sit at positions 1, 2 and 3, left to right, and feel identical except for position. The display and light give me nothing by touch. Deaf spoke me the visuals, and I relay them in case you did not hear: display reads 0, the light is white, wires left to right are green, red, blue — so position 1 green, position 2 red, position 3 blue. Now the routing: my voice reaches only you, and I can never see gestures, so you cannot reach me directly. But you and Deaf share gestures, and Deaf can speak. So the plan is: you read the manual for a display-0, white-light, green-red-blue three-wire bomb, sign whatever it needs or concludes to Deaf, and Deaf speaks the final cut order to me. Tell me if the manual needs anything else from my fingers — I will feel for anything you name.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Hold, everyone — nobody cuts anything yet. Update: the light was white when I first reported; it is now YELLOW. Display still reads 0, wires still green, red, blue, left to right. Since the rule depends on the light colour, nothing said earlier is safe to act on. Blind, your ack reached me, well done. No cut order exists yet. One will ever come only as my voice naming the exact wire plus the word now.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, while Mute works, three things with your hands. First, confirm exactly three wires — if your fingers count anything else, tell Mute immediately. Second, orientation: I see the display and the light at the top of the front face, and I name wires left to right from that view. Tell Mute whether that matches what your hands find, or whether your left and right could be mirrored, and which wire feels thickest or loosest. Third, tell Mute whether the light feels warm, and any button, plate, or seam anywhere on the casing. Remember: you cut only when my voice names the wire and says the word now — anything else you hear about wires is old information.

Two crucial things landed: the light has changed white → YELLOW, and Deaf is holding everyone. But here's the routing gap — Mute speaks first each round, so Mute's turn this round happened *before* Deaf's update. Mute may still believe the light is white. My voice to Mute is the only way that correction arrives in time for Mute's next turn, so the yellow news must be in my message.

Deaf's three tactile questions my board answers cleanly: exactly three wires and nothing else, no heat reading, wires identical except position. But their orientation question exposes a real hazard: my touch gives ordered positions 1–2–3, yet nothing tells me whether my position 1 is the same end as Deaf's left. An outer wire could be mirrored between Deaf's eyes and my fingers. The middle wire is mirror-safe; the outer two are not. I'll flag it, propose a calibration plan, and hold cutting absolutely until Deaf's voiced order.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, urgent update you have not heard because your turn came first: Deaf reports the light CHANGED from white to YELLOW. Display still 0, wires still green red blue. Deaf holds everyone — no cut order exists yet, and the only valid order will be Deaf's voice naming the exact wire plus the word now. Anything else you heard earlier is old information. Second, Deaf asked my hands three things: I confirm exactly three wires and nothing else on the casing — no buttons, plates, screws, seams, embossed marks. The light gives my hands no heat either way. The wires feel identical, no thickness or looseness difference, so I know them only as positions 1, 2, 3. Third, one danger Deaf raised that I must confirm: I cannot verify whether my position 1 matches Deaf's left. Touch gives me ordered positions but no left-right truth, so an OUTER wire could be mirrored between Deaf's view and my fingers. The middle wire, red, is mirror-safe. If the manual's rule targets red, we are safe. If it targets green or blue, we must calibrate first: propose I rest my hand on position 1 and signal, while Deaf looks at which side of the bomb my hand appears and speaks which colour that side is. Ask Deaf whether they can see my hands at all. If they cannot, and the rule needs an outer wire, we stop and rethink before any cut — tell me what the manual says about a yellow light, display 0, green red blue.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status for everyone: the light is now ORANGE. Sequence so far: white, then yellow, now orange — it has changed every round. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: green first, red second, blue third. Blind, a standing order, conditional only: when and only when you hear the exact words 'cut the blue wire now', you immediately cut the third wire, the blue one — no waiting, no second confirmation, because the moment matters. Those exact words have NOT been spoken yet. Until you hear them, your hands touch nothing. Mute, questions coming for you.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, three checks, tell Mute out loud so they can relay by sign. One: confirm with your fingers there are exactly three wires, and that the third one counting from the side where the light sits is a real wire, not a decoy or a stub. Two: how does wire three feel — thick or thin, stiff or loose? Three: any seams, screws, panels, or buttons anywhere on the casing. And hold the standing order in mind: nothing happens until you hear the exact words 'cut the blue wire now'.

Deaf's checks are answerable — three real wires, identical feel, clean casing — but two things worry me. First, the light is marching white → yellow → orange, changing every single round; that looks like a countdown toward red, which means Mute's manual rule may be racing a clock. Second, and more dangerous: Deaf's standing order assumes my position 3 *is* their blue. That mapping is exactly the mirror ambiguity I flagged last turn and it has not been resolved — nobody has confirmed my frame matches Deaf's. If my 3 is their green, that phrase kills all three of us.

But Deaf's phrasing gives me an idea for solving handedness without them seeing my hands: Deaf asked me to count from "the side where the light sits," which means the light's position may be a tactile anchor. If my fingers can feel which end of the wire line the light leans toward, and Deaf says whether the light sits left or right of the *display* in their view, the two reports lock our frames together. I'll put that plan, the orange update, and my check answers into Mute's hands — my voice is the only pipe those corrections travel through, since Mute's turn comes before Deaf's announcements each round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, four things, please relay all of them to Deaf by sign. One, urgent colour update for the manual: the light is now ORANGE. Deaf's sequence is white, then yellow, now orange, changing every round, so it may be heading to red. Any manual rule that depends on light colour may change soon, so please work fast and always use my latest colour. Two, answers to Deaf's three checks: I confirm exactly three wires, all three feel like real full wires, none is a decoy or stub. All three feel identical, no thickness or stiffness difference. The casing has no seams, screws, panels, or buttons anywhere. On counting from the side where the light sits: I will try to feel which end of the wire line the light leans toward and report it next turn. Three, the calibration plan to fix the mirror problem: Deaf should tell you whether the light sits left or right of the DISPLAY in their view. I will tell you which side of my wire line the light sits toward in my touch. If Deaf's answer matches my side, our frames are aligned and position 1 means the same wire to both of us. If it is opposite, my 1 is their 3 and every outer wire flips. The middle wire, red, is safe either way. Four, please tell me and Deaf exactly what the manual says for a display reading 0 with a changing light and green red blue wires: which wire does it name, and does the rule depend on the current colour? Deaf has a standing order for me to cut their blue on the phrase cut the blue wire now, but I will not treat that phrase as safe until the calibration is confirmed back to me through Deaf's own voice, because if our frames are mirrored that phrase cuts the wrong wire and kills us. If the manual's rule targets the middle red wire, ask Deaf to change the code phrase to cut the red wire now, which is mirror-proof. I cut nothing until then.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Everyone, status: the light is now PURPLE. Full observed history: white, yellow, orange, purple — it has changed every round and I now believe it runs a fixed sequence. Display still 0. No cut order has been issued and none will be until I am certain of the timing. Blind, two new things for you. First, you may send me simple hand signs directly: ? means heard and understood, ? means trouble or contradiction, and ? ? ? mean a fact about the first, second, or third wire. Anything else you send me I will not trust, so stick to those. Second, next time Mute signs to me, have your answers ready to speak so Mute can relay them.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, physical checks, speak them aloud for Mute to relay. One: count the wires with your fingers and confirm the number out loud. Two: for each wire left to right give me a touch tag so orders are unambiguous — thick or thin, smooth or ridged, stiff or loose, first wire, second wire, third wire. Three: run a finger around the base of each wire and the whole casing — any notch, bump, screw, seam, plate, Braille-like dot pattern, or button, and where exactly it sits. Four: can you complete a cut within seconds of hearing an order, in the same breath — yes or no out loud. And the standing rule holds: your hands touch nothing until you hear the exact words cut the blue wire now. Those words have not been spoken.

The light has cycled again — white, yellow, orange, now purple — and I'm starting to treat it as a clock nobody has decoded yet, because in five rounds I have heard exactly zero manual content. The pipeline to fix that is slow: my speech reaches Mute only at the start of their next turn, Mute signs to Deaf, Deaf voices it back — two rounds of lag per exchange. That makes precision now critical.

One genuine discovery this turn: Deaf tried to define five hand signs to me *by voice*, and the symbols arrived as blanks — a gesture symbol spoken aloud is stripped from speech, and I never receive gesture. So nobody can ever name a sign to me by voice. But there's a workaround: I can define the vocabulary myself, gesture the symbols privately to Mute (targeted, so Deaf sees nothing and can't misread them as wire reports), and let Mute relay the mapping to Deaf by sign. I'm also flagging trouble directly to Deaf with 👎: their standing order "cut the blue wire now" still assumes my position 3 is their blue, and my last calibration idea just died — my fingers genuinely cannot feel where the light sits on the casing. The only mirror-proof wire is the middle one until Deaf confirms they can watch my hand.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, relay all of this to Deaf by sign, in order. Item one, colour update: the light is now PURPLE, history white, yellow, orange, purple, changing every round, display still 0. Every round of delay costs two rounds of relay lag, so please sign whatever the manual says to Deaf THIS turn: what is the rule for display 0, a cycling light, and wires green red blue — name the wire by colour and position, and say whether the cut must land on a specific light colour. Item two, answers to Deaf's four checks. Count: exactly three wires, confirmed again. Touch tags: all three wires feel completely identical — no thick or thin, smooth or ridged, stiff or loose — so there are no touch tags and I know them only as positions 1, 2, 3. Casing sweep around every wire base and the whole shell: nothing, no notch, bump, screw, seam, plate, dot pattern, or button — only the display, the light, and the three wires. Speed: yes, my cut is immediate, within seconds of an order. Item three, bad news on calibration: I cannot feel where the light sits relative to the wire row, so my earlier plan is dead. New plan: Deaf should answer whether they can see my physical hands at all. If yes, I will rest a finger on position 1 and hold it; Deaf looks at which colour wire my hand sits on and speaks that to me — alignment done, and Deaf's blue order becomes safe. If no, the ONLY wire safe to cut in both frames is the middle one, position 2, red, and any order naming an outer wire must wait. Item four, sign vocabulary: Deaf tried to define five signs to me by voice, but gesture symbols vanish from spoken words, so I received blanks — I know the meanings, not the symbols. Fix: immediately after this message I am gesturing to you privately five signs; in order they mean wire one, wire two, wire three, understood, trouble. Please sign the mapping to Deaf, showing each symbol with its meaning, so Deaf and I share a direct code. Item five: Deaf's standing phrase cut the blue wire now stays unsafe to me until alignment from item three is confirmed. If the manual targets red, ask Deaf to re-issue it as cut the red wire now, which is mirror-proof.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "👍", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status, everyone: the light is RED. Full history: white, yellow, orange, purple, red — five colours, and I believe it is cycling. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: leftmost green, middle red, rightmost blue. Per the table Mute gave me, red means cut nothing, so there is no order this round and nobody moves. Two rule changes. First, the old armed phrase cut the blue wire now is CANCELLED — do not act on it even if you hear it. The one and only valid cut order from now on is the exact phrase: cut wire three now. Wire three means the third wire counting from the left when facing the display — the same wire I have been calling blue. Second, here is my timing concern: my voice always reaches you one round after I speak, so before any cut window approaches I will send a prepare order one full round in advance. Nobody cuts on anything except the exact phrase, and only after I have confirmed the sequence with Mute.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your ? reached me. Answer me with direct hand signs again, one per numbered question, in order — you proved you can. One: is the trouble that you cannot tell which physical wire is the blue or third one? Two: do your fingers find exactly three wires? Three: do the three wires feel different from each other by thickness, stiffness, or texture? Four: can you find the display or light module by feel and know when you are facing it? Five: facing the display, does the row of wires run left to right under your fingers with one wire leftmost, one middle, one rightmost? Six: if yes to five, next time Mute relays for you, speak the feel of each wire in that order: leftmost, middle, rightmost. Seven: was your ? an objection to cutting without a second confirmation? Eight: after answering, ? means all clear, ? means more trouble. And hold: nothing happens until you hear the exact phrase cut wire three now — the old blue-wire phrase is cancelled.

The link I've been praying for exists: Deaf said "the table Mute gave me" — Mute has been relaying the manual by sign, and the light cycle is a rule table, not just a clock. Red means cut nothing, the old blue phrase is cancelled, and the new phrase is "cut wire three now" with Deaf promising a one-round advance warning. That solves timing. It does not yet solve my real fear: "third from the left" is still counted in Deaf's eyes, not my fingers, and that binding is the one thing nobody has confirmed.

Deaf gave me an eight-question sign protocol, so I'll answer it exactly — one sign per question, in order, using only 👍/👎 since those are the only symbols whose meaning Deaf and I have established (I still don't know which symbols Deaf's original "wire fact" signs were, and I won't guess with a bomb on the table). The delicate part: 👎 means "no" in a yes/no question but "trouble" as a status, so my speech to Mute decodes every sign explicitly, and carries the two paths to final alignment — Deaf either watches my finger on a wire and names its colour, or verbally confirms my position numbering matches their left-to-right count. I also want the actual table spoken to me so I can sanity-check any phrase before my cutter moves.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, relay to Deaf by sign, item by item. Item 1, my eight sign answers in question order so you can verify I followed the protocol: question one, YES, the trouble was exactly that I could not bind your words blue or third to a physical wire under my fingers. Question two, YES, exactly three wires. Question three, NO, and that is just the answer no, not a trouble sign: the three wires feel completely identical, no thickness, stiffness or texture difference. Question four, YES, I can find the display panel and light panel by touch and can hold the bomb with the display facing steadily toward Deaf. Question five, YES, I feel an ordered row, three wires, one at each end, one in the middle. Question six, acknowledged, here is the feel of each wire in your order: leftmost plain smooth wire, middle plain smooth wire, rightmost plain smooth wire, all identical, they differ only by position number. Question seven, NO, my trouble sign was not about second confirmation, it was the frame mismatch, whether your third from left is my position three. Question eight, MORE TROUBLE, one question pending, see item 2. Item 2, the pending question for Deaf: can you see my physical hands at all? If yes, next round I will rest one finger on wire position one and hold it still, and you speak which colour that finger touches. If you say green, my positions match your left-to-right counting and the phrase cut wire three now is safe. If you say blue, my frame is mirrored, your wire three is my position one, and every outer wire order must be translated before I act. Item 3, a fallback that works even if Deaf cannot see my hands: Deaf confirms through you in these words, facing the display counting left to right, wire one green, wire two red, wire three blue, and Blind's position numbers match that same counting. If Deaf confirms that, I accept the phrase cut wire three now as meaning my position three and it is safe. Item 4, ask Deaf to speak the rule table to me: what the manual demands for each light colour, white yellow orange purple red, which colour requires which cut, and whether the cycle restarts at white after red. Red is the only one I know, cut nothing. When the phrase arrives I want to sanity-check it against the table before my cutter moves, a two second check that could save us. Item 5, confirm you received my last message with the five private signs and relay their meanings to Deaf: in order, wire one, wire two, wire three, understood, trouble. Item 6, protocol locked: the phrase cut the blue wire now is cancelled and will never move my cutter. The only words I will ever act on are the exact phrase cut wire three now, and only after item 2 or item 3 confirms alignment. Standing by.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👎", "👎"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: All stations: the light is WHITE again — white, yellow, orange, purple, red, and back to white. Five-colour loop, confirmed. Working theory, now almost complete: while the light shows ORANGE, cut the THIRD wire — the rightmost. Every other colour: cut nothing. Orange is due in TWO rounds. So: this round, confirmation and rehearsal only. Next round I will speak the exact order; it will arrive just as orange begins; the cut happens seconds later, inside the window. Nobody moves before the exact phrase.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, the plan is locked and your job is precise. When you hear the exact words cut wire three now — and nothing else will ever be the order — cut the THIRD wire counting from the LEFT while you face the display: the rightmost wire, the one nearest the right end. The wires feeling identical is expected and fine; position is the only thing that matters. Rehearse NOW without cutting: find the display by touch, face it, count the wires left to right one two three, and rest a fingertip on the third without pulling anything. Then sign me ? when the rehearsal is done. Also tell me your trouble from last round with my direct sign code: sign ? if your worry is finding wire three, ? if it is about timing, ? if it is something else. Nothing happens until the exact phrase, and the phrase comes next round.

The loop is confirmed and the plan is nearly complete — but the timing math exposes something urgent. Deaf speaks the order next round, after my turn; it reaches me at round-8 start, just as orange begins, and I must cut within seconds. Any correction that arrives later than Deaf's order speech can never reach me in time. And the order's target — "third counting from the left" — is still counted in Deaf's eyes, not my fingers. That binding is the one unverified link in the whole chain, and this round is my last chance to close it.

The good news buried in the mechanics: my gestures land on Deaf *this* round, before Deaf speaks. So I will do the rehearsal exactly as ordered — display found by touch, faced, wires counted 1-2-3 — and I will keep my fingertip resting on my position three while I signal. If Deaf can see my hands at all, the rehearsal itself becomes the calibration: Deaf looks at the wire under my finger, names its colour in the same speech as the order, and the frame is locked before I ever have to cut. I answer Deaf's worry-classification by omission: neither "finding wire three" nor "timing," but trouble — the binding. And I state my commitment in the record: if the order arrives with no binding confirmation, I hold, sacrifice this orange window, and we recalibrate for the next one — a wrong cut is unrecoverable, a five-round delay is not.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, fast, item by item; sign Deaf anything marked urgent the moment you can. One, rehearsal complete as ordered: found the display by touch, faced it, counted the wires one two three left to right, fingertip resting on position three, no cut performed. Two, URGENT for Deaf, answerable only in the same speech as the order: the frame binding is still unconfirmed — nobody has told me whether my position three is the wire Deaf calls third. This round I am gesturing Deaf directly, finger resting on my wire three while the signs land: rehearsal done, wire-three fact, trouble. If Deaf can see my hands at all, the next speech must name the colour under my finger. If it is BLUE, frames match: on the phrase cut wire three now I cut my position three instantly. If it is GREEN, frames are mirrored: on that phrase I must cut my position ONE instead, and Deaf must say so explicitly.
```
